subject: Redwood trial runbook & KPI commitments for DatumAI evaluation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Ellis Green <ellis.green@datumai.com>; Priya Shah <priya.shah@datumai.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-20T14:00:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood trial runbook & KPI commitments for DatumAI evaluation

Hi Ellis / Priya —

Great to meet on the call earlier. As promised, heres a concise recap and a proposed runbook for the two-week evaluation so we can lock success criteria and ownership quickly. Please reply with any edits and confirm a kickoff slot (I suggested 2027-05-03 below).

High-level goal:
- Validate Redwood inference for DatumAIs real-time summarization pipeline (customer support transcripts) at production-like scale while meeting latency and cost targets.

Proposed success criteria (we want these signed-off before we start):
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end generation <= 250 ms for 1–2k token prompts (measured at Redwood edge).
- Throughput: Sustained 120 concurrent requests / 2k RPS aggregated with <5% error rate during load window.
- Cost: Target gross token cost <= $0.0035 per input+output token with recommended quantization and batching profile.
- Quality: Human evaluation pass-rate >= 88% on a 300-sample blind set (precision/recall/qualitative score).

Evaluation plan (summary):
1) Data & prompts: Well use the sample-prompt-set.csv attached (200 canonical prompts + 100 adversarial cases).
2) Baseline: Run your current endpoint (control) vs Redwoods recommended model variant (open-llama-70b-q4 + cache profile) for apples-to-apples comparison.
3) Load tests: Day 4 run a 2-hour soak with synthetic replay to emulate peak traffic; Day 8 run peak RPS sweep.
4) Quality: Blind scoring on 300 items (50 internal baseline checks + 250 customer samples) with rubric attached in redwood-kpi-template.xlsx.
5) Reporting: We will deliver a short results deck + per-route token/cost breakdown and latency histograms within 48 hours of each test.

Timeline & ownership:
- Kickoff (sync): 2027-05-03 (propose 10am PT) — Sean (AE) / Ellis (DatumAI PM) / Laura (SE) / Monica (CS).
- Setup & ingest: 48 hours (Laura + DatumAI infra contact).
- Tests & scoring: 2 weeks elapsed from kickoff (tests scheduled mid-week to avoid weekend noise).
- Final review: 48 hours after last test run — results + recommendations.

Attachments: trial-runbook-datumai.pdf, sample-prompt-set.csv, redwood-kpi-template.xlsx (see Drive links above).

Immediate asks:
- Ellis: confirm KPI thresholds above or propose modifications by EOD 2027-04-22.
- Priya: note any procurement windows that would affect hardware or signing timelines.
- Laura/Monica: confirm resource availability for May 3 kickoff.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference | +1 415-555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood trial runbook & KPI commitments for DatumAI evaluation

Sean — quick internal notes (taking Lauras SE hat on):

Thanks for the draft. A few technical clarifications we should surface to DatumAI before kickoff: 
- Model variant: open-llama-70b-q4 will likely meet quality but cost might be tight; I recommend we include open-llama-13b-int8 as a lower-cost comparator in the run (same prompts).
- Latency: 250 ms P95 is achievable at small sequence lengths but for 2k-token responses the P95 target should be explicitly measured at both 512/2k lengths to avoid surprises.
- Throughput: the ask for 120 concurrent requests at 2k RPS is ambiguous. Do they mean 120 concurrent clients or 2k RPS overall? Need to confirm: 120 concurrent clients with average 1 request/sec per client ~= 120 RPS, whereas 2k RPS is much higher.
- Cost calc: rough estimate based on our standard q4 profile: 2k tokens round-trip at q4 / 70b -> ~$0.0048/token gross; with batching + q4_0 quantization + prefix KV caching we can likely get net token cost to ~ $0.0032/token. I'll include a short cost model in the runbook PDF.

Proposed additions to the runbook:
- Explicit per-length SLA buckets (<=512, 513–2048).
- A small smoke test step (Day 1) to validate credential/ingest and warm the KV cache before full load.
- Measurement templates (latency histograms, p95/p99, token counts, cost per minute).

I attached a short note to include in the Drive runbook and will prepare the cost table by EOD.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.inference

Thanks for the detailed note, Sean — this is exactly the level of clarity we need. A few quick confirmations from our side: 

- KPI adjustments: were comfortable splitting the latency buckets (<=512 tokens target P95 <= 160 ms; 513–2048 tokens target P95 <= 250 ms).
- Throughput clarification: we mean 2k RPS overall during the peak sweep (our busiest internal ingestion point), not 120 concurrent clients. Apologies for the confusion.
- Cost: target of $0.0035/token is our ceiling; if optimizations land below that were happy.

Procurement heads-up: looping in Priya (cc) — our standard trial procurement window is 30 days for any reserved capacity discussions; well try to keep the initial evaluation to hosted capacity but may request a Dedicated quote depending on results. Priya, can you confirm there are no contractual blockers for a May start?

I can confirm availability for kickoff on 2027-05-03 at 10am PT. Well also provide a 300-sample blind set (sanitized) by 2027-04-27.

Thanks — Ellis
